lines.trans: What a view from up here—you can see the whole courtyard tree and Jasmine Street!
Solid seasoned oak along this entire railing; not a single loose bolt anywhere.
Look at these four iron rings along the beam—spaced exactly two metres apart.
So thirty summers ago, they really hung four golden lines down toward the courtyard tree!
Feel how smooth the inside of this iron ring is from old hemp rope, Rami.
If we angle two lines left and two lines right, every table gets warm light.
How high above Mazen and his head will the lowest lantern hang, Rami?
Three full metres clear—even if Mazen jumps for joy, his glasses are safe!
Speaking of the boss, why has he stayed inside Room Nine since eight this morning?
He bought a giant roll of white poster paper and a bottle of blue ink!
Uh-oh—is he drawing an official anniversary seating chart for twenty-eight guests?
Mark my words, Nour: loose poster paper and Friday wind never end quietly.

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Numeral 'four'; short form أربع (arba') directly before a plural noun (أربع طاولات 'four tables').

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Safety in the house is very important.
They arrived safely and securely.

meanings.note: Elative comparative of واطي ('low'). Invariable for gender and number before or after nouns.

examples.trans: Put the chair on the lowest step.
This shelf is lower than the window.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian everyday verb for 'to come' (إجا / بيجي).

examples.trans: You came ten minutes early.
I will come on Friday at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشتري, بيشتري).

examples.trans: Tell me exactly what to buy.
Buy both brass valves together.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جمع.

examples.trans: The family gathers every Friday at noon.
On Friday the street is quiet.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word (from Turkish burgu) for a metal screw.

examples.trans: I tightened the screw with the small screwdriver.
The chair needs a new screw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The table is made of oak wood.
Oak trees are old and strong.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('under, beneath') and standalone ('downstairs').

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: Form V passive/intransitive counterpart to علّق ('to hang something up').

examples.trans: The lantern will hang above the door.
The sign was hung in the hall.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Means 'grandfather' (جدي my grandfather) and in عن جد ('really / seriously') means 'earnestness'.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.
Did you really finish all the work?

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أحبار.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in blue ink.
The ink pen is on the desk.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural حبال (hibaal).

examples.trans: Pull the rope tight on the tree.
We tied the lanterns with a sturdy cord.

meanings.note: Before a noun or clause حتى means 'even' (حتى والغرفة فاضية 'even when the room is empty').

examples.text: حتى والغرفة فاضية، السلك بيرن مرتين.
examples.trans: Even when the room is empty, the wire rings twice.
Even room four's bell went quiet!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The iron gate is locked at night.
Pass me the heavy iron wrench.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحس, بيحس).

examples.text: نتمنى كل ضيف يحس بالراحة هون.
examples.trans: We hope every guest feels at home here.
I felt the warmth the moment I walked in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حلقات.

examples.trans: The brass ring is twenty millimetres wide.
We fitted a new washer on the pipe.

حِفِظ.gloss: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve

meanings.en: to keep safe; hold onto; preserve
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحفظ, بيحفظ).

examples.trans: Old stone holds the warmth until morning.

examples.text: شكرا لأنك حفظت الشنتة طول الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Thank you for keeping the bag safe all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خطوط.

examples.trans: Your handwriting on the card is clear and neat.
Stay with me on the line a second.

خِلِص.gloss: to run out; be finished; end

meanings.en: to run out; be finished; end
meanings.note: Form I intransitive counterpart of transitive خلّص ('to finish something'): خلص الخبز means 'the bread has run out'.

examples.text: يلا نمشي قبل ما يخلص الخبز السخن.
examples.trans: Let's walk over before the hot bread sells out.

examples.text: خلصت القهوة، رح أعمل إبريق جديد.
examples.trans: The coffee ran out; I will make a fresh pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a wooden or iron railing.

examples.trans: The balcony railing is made of oak wood.
Hold the banister as you go down the stairs.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: روس.

examples.trans: My glasses were on my head!

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من السقف الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low ceiling.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Means 'peace', and in يا سلام! expresses delight ('oh wow! / wonderful!').

examples.text: يا سلام عالشمس الدافية بعد المطر!
examples.trans: Oh how lovely, warm sun after the rain!
They live in safety and peace in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سنوية, plural: سنويين).

examples.trans: He writes in the annual Amman tourist guide.

examples.text: عندنا صيانة سنوية للسخان قبل الشتا.
examples.trans: We do annual maintenance on the heater before winter.

meanings.note: Used in جاب سيرة ('to bring up / mention a topic').

examples.text: لا حدا يجيب سيرة الشغل عالعشا!
examples.trans: Nobody bring up work at dinner!
Everyone speaks kindly of you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.en: huge; massive; large in scale or volume
meanings.note: Feminine ضخمة, plural ضخام. Used for big shapes, large crowds, or oversized objects.

examples.trans: They hung a huge lantern in the middle of the courtyard.

examples.text: موج البحر بالصورة كان ضخم كتير.
examples.trans: The sea wave in the picture was very massive.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضواو.

examples.trans: The yellow light beside the bed is warm.
Turn on the light in the hallway, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Before a time noun, طول (tuul) means 'all ... long / throughout' (طول الليل all night long, طول الأسبوع all week).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Names the horizontal rung of a chair/table or the upper crossbar of a frame.

examples.text: سندت رجلي عالعارضة التحتانية تبع الكرسي.
examples.trans: I rested my foot on the lower rung of the chair.

examples.text: علقنا الفانوس بوسط العارضة الخشب فوق القوس.
examples.trans: We hung the lantern from the middle of the wooden beam over the arch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عالية, plural: عاليين).

examples.trans: What is that loud sound upstairs?
The wooden ceiling is high and sunny.

meanings.note: Appreciative Levantine adjective for fine aged wood, stonework, or heritage objects.

examples.text: خشب الجوز العتيق بالبيانو صوته دافي وأصيل.
examples.trans: The vintage walnut wood in the piano has a warm, resonant tone.

examples.text: الباب العتيق رجع جديد بعد الصنفرة والدهان.
examples.trans: The old heritage door looked new again after sanding and painting.

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Marks location ('at, by') and with pronoun suffixes expresses possession: عندي ('I have'), عندك ('you have'), عندنا ('we have').

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Active participle of فلت ('to slip loose'): feminine فالتة, plural فالتين.

examples.text: انتبه، في حبل فالت من الجهة اليمين.
examples.trans: Careful, there is a loose rope on the right side.

examples.text: عقدنا كل الخيوط الفالتة قبل ما يطيروا.
examples.trans: We tied all the loose threads before they blew away.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فرحات.

examples.trans: His eyes shone with joy!
The family's joy is beyond words.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Asks price, quantity, or time (قديش الساعة؟ 'what time is it?') and exclaims degree (قديش هادية! 'how peaceful!').

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.en: hemp fibre; coarse twine used for tying
meanings.note: Masculine collective noun; in Jordan حبل قنب means sturdy natural hemp twine.

examples.text: جبت لفة خيط قنب عشان نربط الزينة.
examples.trans: I brought a roll of hemp twine so we can tie the decorations.

examples.text: القنب أقوى بكتير من الخيط القطن الرفيع.
examples.trans: Hemp cord is much stronger than thin cotton thread.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قناني.

examples.trans: We bought three bottles of fresh milk.
Put the bottle of cold water on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in plain words.
Your words are kind and reassuring.

meanings.note: Versatile Jordanian noun meaning a wrapped parcel (اللفة البيضا), a pastry roll (لفة قرفة, also pl. لفائف), a street/stair turn (عاللفة), or a wrench turn (لفة، لفتين).

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian question word for 'why?'.

examples.trans: Why did the person run off without his bag?
Why do you keep looking at the clock?

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمتار.

examples.trans: The table is ten metres away.
The courtyard is eight metres wide.

meanings.note: Feminine متينة, plural متان. Used for strong rope, thick paper, or solid construction.

examples.text: لازمنا حبل متين يتحمل وزن الفوانيس.
examples.trans: We need a sturdy rope that can bear the weight of the lanterns.
The cardboard is sturdy and doesn't tear easily.

meanings.note: Used for architectural/room floor plans, schedules, and blueprints.

examples.text: رسمنا المخطط الجديد للطاولات بملف الاستقبال.
examples.trans: We drew the new table floor plan in the front-desk folder.

examples.text: حسب المخطط في مكان مريح لست طاولات بالساحة.
examples.trans: According to the layout there is comfortable room for six tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Passive participle adjective (feminine مرخية, plural مرخيين) used for a sagging rope or loose wire.

examples.text: الحبل بالنص شوي مرخي، شده كمان.
examples.trans: The rope in the middle is a bit slack, pull it tighter.

examples.text: خيطان الزينة صارت مرخية بعد الهوا.
examples.trans: The decoration strings became slack after the wind.

meanings.en: distance; physical gap or space between points
meanings.note: Feminine noun (plural مسافات) used for distances on a road or spacing between objects.

examples.text: خلّي مسافة متر بين الفانوس والتاني.
examples.trans: Leave a metre's distance between one lantern and the next.

examples.text: المسافة من البيت للبلد مش بعيدة.
examples.trans: The distance from the house to downtown isn't far.

meanings.note: Standalone معقول! is a classic Jordanian exclamation of amazed disbelief ('No way! / Could it really be?!').

examples.text: معقول! قطار جدي الخشب لسا موجود!
examples.trans: Could it be! Grandfather's wooden train is still around!
The price is reasonable and fair for everyone.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Masculine noun of place (plural مناظر) from نظر ('to look'). Common exclamation: يا سلام على هالمنظر!

examples.text: من الشرفة بنشوف أحلى منظر لعمان وقت الغروب.
examples.trans: From the terrace we see the prettiest view of Amman at sunset.
The lit lanterns made an amazing sight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين).

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Geminate verb (ن-ط-ط) for jumping or hopping over an obstacle.

examples.text: القطة نطت عن الحيط للجنينة بهدوء.
examples.trans: The cat jumped quietly off the wall into the garden.

examples.text: ما بدنا الضيوف ينطوا فوق الكراسي بالممر!
examples.trans: We don't want guests climbing over chairs in the hallway!

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian demonstrative ('this / that'); feminine هادي (haadi), plural هدول (hadool). Before ال- it also contracts to هال-.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (لهون 'to here', من هون 'from here').

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
Stay right here a minute.

meanings.note: Collective ورق ('paper / tree leaves'), singulative ورقة ('a sheet of paper / note'), plural أوراق ('documents / papers').

examples.trans: We use a paper ledger and a pencil.
He wrote a note on a small slip of paper.

meanings.note: Form II verb for distributing flyers, portions, or kitchen tasks.

examples.text: سلمى قعدت عالكرسي ووزعت الشغل عالكل.
examples.trans: Salma sat in the chair and assigned tasks to everyone.

examples.text: نور وزعت كروت الدعوة عجيران الحارة.
examples.trans: Nour handed out invitation cards to the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: With two pronunciations in context: walla ('or' in choice questions: عالشارع ولا عالساحة؟) and wala ('not even / nor': ولا خدش 'not a single scratch', ولا يهمك 'do not worry at all').

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational bridge introducing an inference ('so that means...'), clarification, or gentle pause ('I mean...').

examples.trans: So the house says hello by itself?
Does that mean there is no heating tonight?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.
